You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 639a82434f16a6df0ce0e7c8595976f1293940fd Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Sven Eckelmann <sven@narfation.org>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2020 07:25:06 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] mtd: parser: cmdline: Fix parsing of part-names with colons

Some devices (especially QCA ones) are already using hardcoded partition
names with colons in it. The OpenMesh A62 for example provides following
mtd relevant information via cmdline:

  root=31:11 mtdparts=spi0.0:256k(0:SBL1),128k(0:MIBIB),384k(0:QSEE),64k(0:CDT),64k(0:DDRPARAMS),64k(0:APPSBLENV),512k(0:APPSBL),64k(0:ART),64k(custom),64k(0:KEYS),0x002b0000(kernel),0x00c80000(rootfs),15552k(inactive) rootfsname=rootfs rootwait

The change to split only on the last colon between mtd-id and partitions
will cause newpart to see following string for the first partition:

  KEYS),0x002b0000(kernel),0x00c80000(rootfs),15552k(inactive)

Such a partition list cannot be parsed and thus the device fails to boot.

Avoid this behavior by making sure that the start of the first part-name
("(") will also be the last byte the mtd-id split algorithm is using for
its colon search.

Fixes: eb13fa022741 ("mtd: parser: cmdline: Support MTD names containing one or more colons")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Cc: Ron Minnich <rminnich@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Sven Eckelmann <sven@narfation.org>
Signed-off-by: Miquel Raynal <miquel.raynal@bootlin.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-mtd/20201124062506.185392-1-sven@narfation.org

diff --git a/drivers/mtd/parsers/cmdlinepart.c b/drivers/mtd/parsers/cmdlinepart.c
index a79e4d866b08..0ddff1a4b51f 100644
--- a/drivers/mtd/parsers/cmdlinepart.c
+++ b/drivers/mtd/parsers/cmdlinepart.c
@@ -226,7 +226,7 @@ static int mtdpart_setup_real(char *s)
 		struct cmdline_mtd_partition *this_mtd;
 		struct mtd_partition *parts;
 		int mtd_id_len, num_parts;
-		char *p, *mtd_id, *semicol;
+		char *p, *mtd_id, *semicol, *open_parenth;
 
 		/*
 		 * Replace the first ';' by a NULL char so strrchr can work
@@ -236,6 +236,14 @@ static int mtdpart_setup_real(char *s)
 		if (semicol)
 			*semicol = '\0';
 
+		/*
+		 * make sure that part-names with ":" will not be handled as
+		 * part of the mtd-id with an ":"
+		 */
+		open_parenth = strchr(s, '(');
+		if (open_parenth)
+			*open_parenth = '\0';
+
 		mtd_id = s;
 
 		/*
@@ -245,6 +253,10 @@ static int mtdpart_setup_real(char *s)
 		 */
 		p = strrchr(s, ':');
 
+		/* Restore the '(' now. */
+		if (open_parenth)
+			*open_parenth = '(';
+
 		/* Restore the ';' now. */
 		if (semicol)
 			*semicol = ';';
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/mtd/parsers/cmdlinepart.c`**
1. **Variable Declaration**: Added a new variable `open_parenth` to store the position of the first opening parenthesis `(` in the string.
2. **String Manipulation**: 
   - Before determining the `mtd_id`, the code now checks for the presence of an opening parenthesis `(` and replaces it with a null character `\0` to isolate the `mtd_id` from the partition names.
   - After finding the last colon `:`, the code restores the opening parenthesis back to its original position.
3. **Comment Addition**: Added comments to clarify the purpose of the changes, specifically to ensure that part-names containing colons are not incorrectly treated as part of the `mtd_id`.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in `cmdlinepart.c` are directly related to fixing a bug in the parsing logic for MTD (Memory Technology Device) partition names that include colons. The original parsing logic incorrectly split the `mtd_id` and partition names when colons were present, leading to boot failures for devices with such partition names. By isolating the `mtd_id` from the partition names using the position of the first opening parenthesis, the patch ensures that the parsing correctly identifies the partition names, thus preventing the boot failure. The changes are a refinement of the previous logic introduced in commit `eb13fa022741`, which aimed to support MTD names with colons but inadvertently introduced this parsing issue.
